recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if a future work-group decision asks to change the Definition pattern standards status or maturity beyond the paragraph removal requested by this issue.
issue_request: FHIR-14772 was Published/Persuasive for STU3 and asked to resolve a mismatch where the Definition pattern was flagged Informative but its text said it should be treated as draft for comment. The approved resolution was to remove that paragraph.
initial_application: No commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-14772 was found. Git pickaxe history found commit 14b69a1c6dd33918b20d53ffd6cfbab523f840ba removing the exact disputed paragraph from source/definition/definition-spreadsheet-introduction.xml while updating Definition pattern sources, which appears to be the historical application.
additional_context: The Definition logical model remains active in the current build through source/fhir.ini's active [logical] definition entry. Current source/definition/definition-spreadsheet-introduction.xml contains the Definition Background and Context guidance and W5 linkage without the obsolete paragraph. Targeted Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later or conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit because the current authoritative source already implements the approved removal and no source edit is needed.

evidence_items.summary: Published/Persuasive STU3 issue requesting removal of the paragraph that said the Definition pattern was draft for comment despite being flagged Informative.
evidence_items.learned: This is final WG intent and establishes that paragraph removal, not a broader status rewrite, is the approved change.

evidence_items.summary: The current Definition Background and Context section contains the general pattern guidance and W5 linkage but not the disputed draft-for-comment paragraph.
evidence_items.learned: The authoritative source already matches the approved removal.

evidence_items.summary: The active [logical] section lists definition as a logical model.
